title: Elastic admission controller with per-tenant leaky pools and outage fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During sudden tenant-driven bursts and partial limiter outages, our global quota fabric either rejects too-aggressively (causing customer-visible 429s) or accepts unfairly (allowing noisy tenants to exhaust capacity). We need an admission controller that maintains SLOs by smoothing bursts per tenant, preserving weighted fairness across tiers, and providing a deterministic degraded fallback when the central limiter is unavailable.

Goal: Implement an elastic leaky-pool admission controller colocated in regional proxies that: (1) enforces per-tenant soft ceilings with short-term burst absorption, (2) reconciles with central quota state asynchronously, (3) applies tier-aware weighted fairness during contention, and (4) switches to an outage-safe fallback mode that preserves critical customers and SLO quotas without catastrophic global imbalance.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end simulation shows 95th percentile tail latency impact < 10% and SLO error budget consumption within target under a 3x synthetic burst for 10 minutes.
2) Under central limiter outage, the degraded policy maintains proportional throughput across paying tiers (within 15% of steady-state share) and limits total accepted QPS to preconfigured safe cap.
3) No customer experiences repeated back-to-back 429s for >30s unless they exceed their long-term quota.
4) Automated chaos test reproduces dual-region failover while preserving token fairness and emits dashboards/alerts.
proposal: Deploy a local admission controller in each regional proxy that maintains an in-memory per-tenant leaky-pool (approximate token bucket) with two windows: a fast short-window (smoothing for bursts, ~5s) and a slow long-window (enforcement for quota, ~1h). The controller accepts requests if local pool tokens available; it asynchronously consumes tokens from central quota (best-effort). On central connectivity loss, the controller enters 'degraded mode' and applies a deterministic weighted shedding policy: reserve percent for critical tiers, enforce proportional share on remainder via a fast approximation of weighted fair queuing, and expose a graceful 429 response containing retry-after and reason code. Periodically reconcile with central state and apply correction dampening to avoid oscillation.
design_notes:
Core components:
- Per-tenant LeakyPool: dual-window counters implemented with decay counters (exponential sliding window) to avoid hot-key hot-spikes in memory. Lightweight C++ in proxy hot path; exposes metrics.
- Reconciliation Agent: background worker that batches lease updates to central quota service every 1s; uses optimistic local credit draining.
- Degraded Policy: when central unavailable > 500ms or error rate > 5%, flip to regional safe-cap which is precomputed per-region based on historical allocation and capacity. Within safe-cap, use tier-reservations and a folded weighted-fair admission algorithm (approximate with per-tier deficit counters).
- Telemetry: emit per-tenant accepted/rejected counts, token-imbalance gauge, reconciliation lag, degraded-mode reason and duration.
- Backpressure hooks: when admission rejects, propagate a standardized Retry-After header and telemetry tag to help caller adapt.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Clock skew causing credits regeneration: use monotonic clock and bounded regen.
- Hot tenant draining entire pool during degraded mode: apply emergency per-tenant hard-cap and circuit breaker that moves heavy tenants to slow-path with token sampling.
- Oscillation between central reconciliation and local estimates: use dampening factor and incorporate central 'lease epoch' increasing to reject stale corrections.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2w): prototype LeakyPool in regional proxy with unit tests; simulate small-scale bursts locally. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/2743.
Phase 2 (2w): build Reconciliation Agent and central lease API; end-to-end integration tests against central quota simulator. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quota-service/pull/781.
Phase 3 (1w): implement Degraded Policy and tiered reserving; add canary in us-west-2.
Phase 4 (1w): chaos testing (partition central limiter), telemetry dashboards, and runbook. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/512.
Phase 5: gradual rollout (regional canaries -> 25% -> 75% -> global) with automated rollback on SLO delta > 5%.
telemetry_and_tests:
Simulations:
- Synthetic multi-tenant workload with power-law tenant distribution; burst patterns (spikes, churn) and correlated multi-region surges. Stored results: s3://redwood-simulations/elastic-leakypool/2025-02-20/results.csv.
SLOs to monitor:
- 99th pct request latency, 429 rate by tenant tier, reconciliation lag > 1s, degraded-mode duration.
Chaos tests:
- Central limiter partition (3s, 30s, 5m), region pair outage, and slow disk causing reconciliation delays.
Automated unit/integration tests:
- Deterministic token decay tests, weighted fairness convergence tests, and backpressure header propagation checks.
discussion_and_tradeoffs:
Alternatives considered:
- Fully consistent central quota enforcement: higher correctness but increased latency and brittle during partitions. Rejected due to availability risk.
- Stateless admission relying on central cached leases only: simpler but causes unfairness during sustained bursts.
- Local machine-learning estimator for burst prediction: promising but risky in short term; deferred to Optimize team.

Tradeoffs:
- Local admission favors availability and latency but risks temporary global fairness drift; mitigated by conservative safe-cap and dampened reconciliation.
- Complexity increases code path in hot proxy; minimized by small, well-tested C++ module and strict telemetry.
